clue.text: Good — find out Romeo is the one complaining

parts.note: to rumble someone is British slang for discovering what they are up to
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tale of someone finding out that Romeo is the moaner in the relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumbler is a person who habitually moans, so the one complaining fits as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Annual production — of bakery I'd chat about?

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the bakery's yearly output being a matter for gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BAKERYIDCHAT; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake baked to mark each year someone turns older is a yearly creation, made once per year.

clue.text: Spin energy raters conceal

indicators.note: the words energy raters conceal the answer, which runs across the join between them

explanation.surface: People who rate energy are hiding something about spin.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to turn rapidly round a centre, which is a synonym for whirling in circles.

clue.text: Join football administrators' team, one short?

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, England's governing body; the possessive adds S
a football team has eleven players, so one short of a team is ten

explanation.surface: An invitation to join a football team run by the FA that is a player down.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the Football Association, which runs English football.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten things is to secure or attach them together, a synonym for join as a verb.

clue.text: Timely midpoint unchanged after revolution

indicators.note: the word reads the same when turned round backwards, so revolving it leaves it unchanged

parts.note: the midpoint of the day by the clock is midday

explanation.surface: A midpoint that stays the same however it is turned.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so the wordplay is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday sits at the middle of the day, so it is the midpoint in terms of time.

clue.text: Clever bishop, unsettled?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation
unsettled weather is showery and wet

explanation.surface: Asking whether a clever bishop is a nervous one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' looks like it describes the bishop's mood, but it refers to the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brainy has plenty of intelligence, making them clever or bright.

clue.text: Person who writes of a universal god

parts.note: U is the film certificate abbreviation for universal
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A writer who chooses to write about a god of all people.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of books or articles is a synonym, the creator of a written work.

clue.text: Describing one-party system — attritional, beginning to age terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled into a fresh order
beginning to picks out the first letter of the word age

explanation.surface: A one-party state is ground down by attrition and starts ageing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to age' gives A, which joins ATTRITIONAL before 'terribly' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A totalitarian regime allows only one ruling party, so the word describes such a system as an adjective.

clue.text: Some freedom, I think, to exclude

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A speaker musing that some freedom may mean leaving things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to exclude it, a straightforward synonym in the infinitive.

clue.text: A titan in North Korea initially finding sort of weapon

indicators.note: in places the giant inside the abbreviation for the country
initially takes the opening letters of North and Korea

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A giant in North Korea discovers a new kind of weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An antitank gun or missile is designed to destroy armoured vehicles, so it names a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Bully unhappy about Director General appearing

indicators.note: about means the word for unhappy goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a performer who is on is appearing on stage

explanation.surface: A miserable Director General turns up and starts throwing their weight around.
explanation.definitionFit: To bludgeon someone is to coerce or intimidate them forcefully, the verb sense of bully.

clue.text: Cereal plant royalty oddly ignored

indicators.note: oddly ignored drops the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of royalty, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A grain crop that royals strangely pay no attention to.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a grain crop grown for food and fodder, so the singular is a cereal plant.

clue.text: Former librarian advising trade exhibition, just starting

indicators.note: just starting takes only the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A retired librarian gives advice about a trade fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The late chairman means the previous one, so late is used for someone or something former.

clue.text: Stream entering the river in type of film?

indicators.note: entering means the word for a stream goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a rill is a small stream
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A brook flowing into a river, as if describing a scene from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspense movie full of excitement is one genre of cinema; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Multitude, crazy, leaderless

indicators.note: leaderless removes the first letter, the one at the head

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A huge, wild crowd with no one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An army can mean any vast number of people or things, as in an army of fans.

clue.text: Unusual step — rest in Church in Rome

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are put in an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd move: taking a break in a Roman church.
explanation.definitionFit: The great basilica in the Vatican City is the famous Roman church named after the apostle.

clue.text: Hut song

definitions.meaning: a sailors' work song sung at sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rough dwelling and a sea song sung by sailors while working.

clue.text: Parking contract to give satisfaction

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: A parking agreement that is supposed to keep customers happy.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight or gratify someone is to give them satisfaction, the verb sense.

clue.text: Get away with a daughter on board for adventure

indicators.note: on board means taken inside, like passengers on a ship

parts.note: to escape is to get away
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A getaway with a daughter along makes for an adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous exploit, a lively adventure.

clue.text: Poles meeting extremely annoying hitch

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

indicators.note: extremely takes the letters at both extremes of the word annoying

explanation.surface: Meeting Polish people gives a very irritating problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected obstacle or difficulty, a synonym for a hitch.

clue.text: Rugby Union — the French hold sway

parts.note: le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Rugby Union dominates in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to govern or dominate, the verb sense of holding sway.

clue.text: On radio, might Catherine briefly be successful?

indicators.note: on radio means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: might, as in it may happen, gives may; Kate is the short form of the name Catherine

explanation.surface: Wondering on air whether Catherine might succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' gives MAY and 'Catherine briefly' gives KATE; 'On radio' says MAY KATE is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make it is the idiom for succeeding or achieving one's goal.

clue.text: Wrongly arrest rubberneck

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A gawping onlooker is mistakenly arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubberneck is a gawper who gapes at things, someone who gazes fixedly.
